$comment: Hand-curated deltas over the extracted requirements ledger.
See .requirements/README.md — this file is committed; `reconcile` folds it in.
Each entry names WHY the extracted assertion was wrong, with the measurement,
so a future reader can re-check rather than trust.

REQ-persistence-7bc1224d.assertion: A durable-write writer may declare a `rowKey` — and so become eligible for spill replay — only when its idempotency is arbitrated by a real database uniqueness constraint. A writer with no such constraint declares no `rowKey` and is `lost`-only, because at-least-once replay against a non-idempotent writer would corrupt the rows the seam exists to protect.
reason: The extracted assertion read: 'Only audit.findings and audit.runComplete durable writers may declare rowKey values and thereby be eligible for replay, while all other registered audit-store writers remain keyless.'

That is false against the code it cites. Measured 2026-09-04 at 88025501, scripts/lib/audit-store-writers.mjs registers SIX keyed writers: audit.findings (:132), audit.runComplete (:147), audit.convergenceState (:167), audit.diffComplexity (:179), learning.outcome (:191) and debt.entries (:271).
It was extracted from that module's own docstring (:21-28), which still described the two-writer state and had itself gone stale as writers were promoted out of lost-only.
Its cited evidence test contradicts it directly: tests/audit-store-durability-call-site.test.mjs:188-192 records 'upsertDebtEntries: now REGISTERED as debt.entries (2026-08-27)'.

Leaving it active is not harmless: a reader 'restoring' the invariant would strip debt.entries' rowKey and silently reopen the loss it was added to fix — reproduced in a consumer 2026-08-27 at 228 local entries against a 197-row mirror.
The replacement states the property the code and the test actually share: a key requires a constraint. debt.entries satisfies it via UNIQUE (repo_id, topic_id).
REQ-persistence-7bc1224d.correctedBy: docs/plans/backlog-and-drift-reduction.md (round-2 audit finding H1, accepted with its direction inverted)

Recorded rather than glossed: a round-1 code audit correctly re-raised the stale assertion as still live (H2/H16). Self-healing regardless: the assertion was EXTRACTED from audit-store-writers.mjs's docstring, and that docstring is now corrected, so the next extract regenerates the right text with or without this file.
